what_happened: Scene L8/S8, same faucet as s4/s8/s22. Here the sponge went first: grasped at 233 and released at 334, dropping ~16 cm into the basin (stage 0 at 348). The pan (pan_5) was grasped by the handle at 460 and placed flat in the basin at 612; the fingers brushed the sponge at 607-614 (stage 1 at 631). Stage 2, first approach 720-860: the gripper pressed against the round spout head (sink contact 770-858; the head fills the wrist view and the lever shows behind or below it). The lever never moved. 880-1120: it hovered upside-down to the left of the faucet with the lever in close view (940-1120), without contact. ~1200: it retreated to the right. 1283-1305: brief contact with the basin rim while looking into the basin. ~1400: another close approach with the lever in view, no contact. 1480-1600: retreat and looking around. The handle stayed at 0.000.
causal_chain: both objects in by 631 (969 steps left) -> first approach hits the spout head (770-858), not the lever -> hovers near the lever 880-1120 without touching -> retreat / re-approach (~1400) / retreat cycle -> lever never moved, water off at 1600
self_recovery: Several re-approaches to the faucet (880-1120, ~1400). None touched the lever.
official_criterion_notes: The sink contact intervals mix spout-head (770-858) and basin-rim (1283-1305) contacts. Objects stayed in the basin.
uncertain_about: Whether 880-1120 was a deliberate hover at the lever or repositioning. The wrist shows the lever within a few cm but no contact.
